questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting location in a nice country with good academics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Decently easy. A lot of work had to be done.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Terrible. Had a mandatory program which was online and cost $250 dollars and did not provide any useful information.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Facebook groups are your friend. Was pretty difficult to find something good. In general it was quite expensive. Be wary of were you live / how far away from campus as some areas are sketchy. If possible, talk to current/prior students about areas. I would recommend living close to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live close to campus. Berkeley has some sketchy areas and in general its nice to be able to walk back and forth. International house and Coops are both solid options but beware some Coops party a lot. Facebook groups are nice for finding roommates.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very very expensive and general poor selection.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Not much except choosing courses and picking up IDs. They have some mandatory online courses/tests which are quite boring.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mostly online ressources.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. Registration opens around october/november, be prepared and ready. If you dont get the courses you want sign up for the waitlist and be ready to swap during the first two weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do your research early and register in October and November as courses get filled up but most have space then. Use the first couple weeks to figure out which classes your really want, and often space opens in all courses if you're on the waitlist.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Undergraduate courses are quite easy, graduate courses are difficult. A balance is nice. In general classes are very good. Take a DeCal course as well, and be ready for the sign up at the start of the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More empirical and interactive. Office hours are nice. Very passionate and engaged professors.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: ECON 230B - Public Economics , ECON 134 Macro Economic Policy from The Great Depression Until Today, Econ 133 Inequality and Growth, Econ 115 World Economy in the 20th Century.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Honestly i really enjoyed all my courses. Especially 230B with Saez. 133 With Zucman is also really interesting.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I tried to waive the insurance with Gouda but was denied mid semester and forced enrolled with a fee of $1888 dollars. Housing was in general super expensive. Surprisingly books for class where almost all free.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was very expensive and hard to grocery shop so difficult to cook for yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Decals for learning new things. Sports clubs for most. Intramural sports as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Play some tennis. Perhaps join some intramural sports. Hike around the firetrails.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: SF. Firetrails. Yosemite. Big Sur. Hearst Castle.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes. Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Little difficult. They're mostly 17-22. Perhaps rush a frat / live in a coop / join some sports league. Decals are good for this as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Most locals 'had their own life' so a little difficult to get in contact wtih them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hospitality and openess.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Search and apply for courses and especially scholarships (Legater) in very good time! Its really worth it. 
Housing live at I-house (And apply in good time as its first come first serve) if you want easy mingling and living with other exchange students, Co-ops if you want to meet locals who like to party and do drugs, Off campus through facebook sites otherwise.
SHIP is very difficult to waive with danish insurance companies. If you wanna waive do it through something like ISO.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy Berkeley and SF. Its a nice place and academics are top notch. Participate and attend. Meet people. Enjoy the sunsets from up the firetrails. Go on trips to the national parks and hike.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Incredible professors. Beautiful country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting everything in order before going. Finding good housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
